bullets.title: June CPI surprise: largest MoM drop in 5 years slashes July hike odds to ~16%
bullets.body: June headline CPI fell -0.35% m/m (survey -0.12%) and core CPI declined -0.02% m/m (consensus +0.23%), the largest month-over-month inflation drop in roughly 5 years. Markets immediately repriced July Fed rate hike probability from ~43% to ~16%, 2-year yields fell ~9 bps, and the EUR rallied above 1.1400. Goldman flags core PCE readthrough at ~+0.18% m/m, dovish for risk but insufficient to fully remove upside inflation risk.

bullets.title: Warsh hawkish at House testimony: skeptical of trimmed-mean metrics, emphasizes price stability mandate
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told the House Financial Services Committee he views existing 'outlier-removing' inflation measures like the Dallas Fed trimmed mean as unreliable guides to underlying inflation, and offered a pointed critique of the 2020 flexible average inflation-targeting framework. He reiterated rate hikes remain an option if broad-based inflation resurfaces, while calling isolated price shocks unlikely to alter policy on their own. Gold settled at $4,054 (+1.3%) as a hedge.

bullets.title: 2Q26 earnings off to a record start: banks dominate, EPS pace implies +27.8% S&P 500 growth
bullets.body: JPM, GS, BAC, Citi, and WFC delivered broad Q2 beats; JPM posted record net income of $21B (+40% YoY) with equities revenues up 86%, GS beat consensus by ~45%. 75% of S&P 500 reporters topped estimates; UBS estimates S&P 500 EPS on pace for +27.8% YoY growth once historical revision trends are applied. TECH+ expected to grow +47.7% EPS vs S&P 500 +22.0%, led by NVDA (+97.3%) and GOOGL (+26.1%).

bullets.title: AI/momentum unwind deepening: HF net leverage hits 39th percentile, Broad AI exposure at YTD low
bullets.body: Global fundamental L/S managers are down ~-3% MTD on negative long-side alpha, reversing ~75% of cumulative net buying since April. Gross leverage fell in 5 of the last 6 weeks (75th percentile on 3-yr lookback) while net leverage dropped ~7 pts from a 4-year high. Info Tech and Comm Services led net selling, with Mag7 and Semiconductor/Tech Hardware most net sold. Goldman notes the Broad AI exposure basket has fallen to its lowest YTD level and recommends buying the dip in hyperscalers and data center equipment.

bullets.title: US-Iran military conflict escalates: blockade resumed, strikes on power infrastructure threatened
bullets.body: US Central Command resumed airstrikes against Iran at 3pm ET and reinstated a naval blockade of Iranian ports by 4pm ET, targeting missile/drone sites near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump threatened to strike Iranian power plants and bridges next week if Tehran refuses to negotiate. Brent crude settled at $84.73/bbl (+1.72%); WTI at $79.34 (+1.54%). Persian Gulf flows are estimated down to below 50% of normal, leaving a potential 13.4 mb/d supply gap. GS base case holds Brent at $80 for 4Q26 but flags near-term upside risk above $110 if Gulf recovery disappoints.

bullets.title: China Q2 GDP misses at 4.3% YoY; no major stimulus expected but PBOC cuts likely in H2
bullets.body: China Q2 GDP grew 4.3% YoY, below the 4.5% consensus and the government's 4.5-5.0% target, the weakest pace since late 2022. June retail sales beat at +1.0% YoY (vs -0.1% est.), industrial output +5.3% YoY (vs 4.6% est.), but fixed investment fell 5.7% YTD YoY (worse than -5% est.). JPM and Goldman note Beijing will not announce major new fiscal stimulus but will direct local government spending acceleration; PBOC rate cuts likely in H2. CNY expected to weaken by year-end, with stability maintained through Xi's expected September US visit.

bullets.title: Semiconductor index (SOX) at 20% of S&P 500 weighting, daily oversold near-term but monthly mega-overbought
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks now represent an all-time high 20% of S&P 500 index weight. Technically, the SOX daily momentum is oversold with near-term excesses worked off, setting up a tactical bounce; however, the sector remains 'mega overbought' on weekly and monthly timeframes. Semiconductor volatility is at its highest since 2020, and SEMI trade body raised 2026 equipment sales forecast to $165.9B (+23.2% YoY) from a prior $145B estimate on AI-driven demand.

bullets.title: ASML Q2 beats, raises FY26 guide to €44B on AI EUV demand surge; 2027 capacity at ~85 tools
bullets.body: ASML reported Q2 revenues of €9.33B (consensus €8.85B) with 54% gross margins, and raised FY26 guidance to €44B midpoint vs prior €38B and consensus €39.3B. Q3 guidance of €11-12B was ~11% above Street. ASML is planning a 30% increase in Low-NA EUV capacity to ~85 tools in 2027 and investigating ~110 tools in 2028. The buyside had expected 90-100 units in 2027, leaving capacity guidance as a mild disappointment. Intel is now in high-volume High-NA production.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI question dominates macro narrative; hyperscaler bond spreads at record wides
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags that 'AI is currently driving macro' rather than the reverse, with the key question being when investors will require visible ROI on massive hyperscaler capex spending. Morgan Stanley estimates 80GW of new compute capacity through 2028 requiring $4-8T in capex funded via debt/equity issuance. Hyperscaler bond basket spreads hit record wides, and $107B in debt issuance by hyperscalers YTD is pressuring credit markets. Amazon's $25B bond sale alone pressured hyperscaler debt spreads and Treasuries.

bullets.title: Data center capacity headwinds: $286B in projects cancelled/delayed, NY enacts 1-year ban
bullets.body: An estimated $156B in data center projects were cancelled or delayed in 2025, with a further $130B in Q1 2026 amid community pushback and state-level moratoriums. New York became the first state to enact a one-year ban on new hyperscale data center construction (50+ MW facilities). State-level moratorium bills are also pending in other jurisdictions. PJM failed to clear 7GW needed for 2028 grid stability, and electricity prices would be 70% higher without price caps.

bullets.title: Global semiconductor equipment WFE forecasts rising to $200B+ through 2028 on pricing power
bullets.body: UBS raised price targets on AMAT to $705, LRCX to $435, and KLAC to $255, projecting ~5% cumulative ASP growth through C2028E (potential 10% upside). At $300B WFE, stocks trade at 16x/19x/22x respectively. SEMI's trade body revised 2026 WFE forecast to $165.9B. Blayne at Jefferies raised C26-C28 WFE to $152B/$200B/$253B. Terafab's potential $300-500B capex spend within 4-5 years could reset industry ceiling.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 earnings Thursday: consensus sees NT$1.27T revenue, net profit +59%, gross margin >68%
bullets.body: TSMC reports Thursday July 16 with expectations for Q2 revenue of NT$1.27T, net profit up 59% to NT$632.6B (~US$19.6B)—its 10th consecutive quarter of profit growth—and gross margin forecast above 68%. Google's Pixel 11 is reportedly leading the 2nm node ramp. ASML confirmed TSMC as a DUV/immersion customer driving strong equipment demand in 2026.

bullets.title: Korea KOSPI surged 6.2% on CPI data; 1.2M leveraged accounts had triggered margin calls
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI surged 6.2% overnight after a 9% drop Monday, with Samsung Electronics +7% and SK Hynix +10%, as the soft US CPI print eased global rate-hike fears. KOSDAQ activated a sidecar (trading halt) after 150 futures surged 6%. JPM notes momentum factor z-score is only ~-0.4 compared to -1 to -2z levels historically associated with a clean washout, suggesting positioning remains elevated.

bullets.title: Fund manager positioning at highest long since Dec 2024; BofA 'sell signal' triggered at 3.6% cash
bullets.body: Fund managers have built their largest long stock positions since December 2024. Bank of America warns its contrarian 'sell signal' has been triggered as fund manager cash levels fell to 3.6%—near the lowest this century. Top 10 S&P 500 stocks now account for 43% of total index weight, approaching historical concentration peaks.

bullets.title: NVIDIA H200 chip shipments to China have commenced; Vera Rubin on track and in production
bullets.body: A senior US official confirmed NVIDIA has begun shipping H200 AI chips to China, with roughly 10 Chinese firms cleared including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD, and DeepSeek—estimates of up to 200K units vs prior 75K. Separately, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang confirmed the next-gen Vera Rubin GPU is already in production and on schedule. Morgan Stanley pegs 1 GW GB200/GB300/Vera Rubin data center capex at $35-49B, with Huang suggesting future 1 GW AI factories could approach $100B.

bullets.title: Apple gets China approval for Alibaba Qwen AI integration into Apple Intelligence
bullets.body: China's Cyberspace Administration cleared Apple Intelligence for iPhone in China with Alibaba's Qwen AI integrated on-device, alongside six other approved mobile generative AI models. Apple is planning to launch Apple Intelligence in China by year-end, continuing work with Alibaba and Baidu. BABA gained +3.7% in pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: Memory shortage accelerating: SLC NAND prices forecast +120-170% H2 2026, HBM4 into 2027
bullets.body: Citi's Korea tech team flagged SLC NAND contract prices are forecast to surge 120-170% H2 2026 vs H1, driven by mature NAND capacity shifting to 3D NAND causing MLC shortage. Samsung is converting an R&D site to a new DRAM factory (~100k wpm), and SK Hynix moved its Yongin PH1 opening to February 2027. Jefferies notes China AI capex forecast raised 23% to $1T through 2030, with Huawei's Ascend 950 at 1,000 TFLOPs. A worst-in-70-year memory shortage is expected through at least 2028.

bullets.title: Soft CPI shifts macro tailwinds back to AI-driven earnings: momentum and price momentum groups favored
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's strategy team notes the CPI beat pushed financial tightening risk into the background, allowing earnings fundamentals to drive returns through Q2 season. AI-driven Earnings Momentum and Price Momentum factor baskets have strong earnings expectations and historically strong beat rates. The Morgan Stanley Broad AI index (MSXXAI) shows <25th percentile of stocks above their 50-day MA, a level historically associated with stronger forward returns when oversold. Yield correlation headwinds for AI stocks should fade if 10-year yields remain range-bound at 4.42-4.62%.

bullets.title: $4.2T in options expire July 17; ETF volumes 19% above YTD average, elevated vol risk into expiry
bullets.body: Citi flagged $4.2T in notional open interest expires on July 17 ($2.7T indices, $659B ETFs, $858B single stocks). ETF options volumes are 19% above the YTD average. 50 options chains were identified with strikes within +/-2% of current price and significant open interest relative to daily volume, creating potential for unusual volatility on expiration day. Single-stock volumes are broadly flat but expected to increase into tech earnings late July/early August.

bullets.title: Foreign Treasury demand surged to $9.37T (2nd-highest ever); US long-term capital inflows doubled in May
bullets.body: Foreign investors boosted US Treasury holdings to $9.37T in May, the second-largest total on record, with Canada as the biggest buyer. Net long-term US capital inflows surged to $232.7B in May from $104.8B in April. Japan's holdings fell from $1.21T to $1.14T while China's rose from $651B to $659B. JPM reduced its 2026 foreign demand forecast from $500B to $450B following the data.
